title: Side-Effect Temporal Coupling in Logic Methods
pattern: A boolean check or query method performs a hidden, unrelated mutation side effect that initializes subsystems, establishing a hidden temporal coupling.
why_bad: It violates Command-Query Separation. Callers expect `check_password` to be safe and idempotent. If called out of order or multiple times, it silently overwrites or corrupts state.
detection: Methods whose names indicate a query (e.g., `check_`, `is_`, `get_`) but modify fields of `self` or initialize global systems inside their bodies.
counterexample: Lazy caching (memoization) where the mutated field is purely an internal performance optimization and does not change the semantic behavior of the object.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 3 ("Side Effects") and Chapter 17 ("G31: Hidden Temporal Couplings").
